question: us-policy-positions:justice-public-safety.raise-juvenile-court-age
definition: yes = the juvenile court handles ordinary offenses through age 17 or older (upper age of juvenile delinquency jurisdiction 17+); no = the upper age is 16 or lower, so 17-year-olds start in adult court. Transfer/waiver for serious crimes does not change the answer.
summarySource: OJJDP Statistical Briefing Book, 'Upper age of juvenile court delinquency jurisdiction' (released 10/6/2025; law as of the end of the 2023 sessions), per-state export; checked against primary code pages for TX, WI, LA (changed 4/19/2024), VT, DC, PR and CNMI, fetched 9/28/2026.

conflicts.readings: OJJDP (law as of end of 2023) lists upper age 17; the current Louisiana Children's Code art. 804 sets it at 16 for acts on or after 4/19/2024. The primary code controls, so the answer is no.
